# Use a stable, widely-used base image for compatibility. Ubuntu 22.04 is a good choice.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set DEBIAN_FRONTEND to noninteractive to prevent prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI libraries, git, certificates, and Python.
# --no-install-recommends reduces image size.
# Python is a required dependency for the LAMMPS CMake build system.
# Cleaning apt cache at the end of the same RUN command reduces layer size.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin \
    ca-certificates \
    python3 \
    python3-pip \
    python-is-python3 \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Clone the LAMMPS source code. The 'develop' branch is used to get the latest version as requested.
# Using --depth 1 for a shallow clone to save space and time.
RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch develop https://github.com/lammps/lammps.git /opt/lammps

# Set the working directory to a dedicated build folder.
WORKDIR /opt/lammps/build

# Configure the LAMMPS build using CMake.
# - PKG_REAXFF=on: Enables the ReaxFF package as required by the 'lammps-reax' application name.
# - BUILD_MPI=yes: Compiles LAMMPS with MPI support, crucial for HPC workloads.
RUN cmake \
    -D PKG_REAXFF=on \
    -D BUILD_MPI=yes \
    ../cmake

# Compile the LAMMPS executable using all available CPU cores to speed up the build.
RUN make -j$(nproc)

# Add the LAMMPS build directory containing the 'lmp' executable to the system's PATH.
# This ensures 'lmp' can be called directly from any location.
ENV PATH /opt/lammps/build:$PATH

# Configure OpenMPI environment variables for better compatibility within containerized environments like Kubernetes/Docker.
# This allows MPI to run as root and disables a shared-memory mechanism that can cause issues.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none

# Create and set a new working directory for running simulations.
WORKDIR /app

# As per instructions, copy all files from the specified ReaxFF example directory into the WORKDIR.
# This stages the required input files for a potential HNS benchmark run.
RUN cp /opt/lammps/examples/reaxff/HNS/* .

# Set a default command. This will execute if the container is run without a command,
# providing basic information about the LAMMPS executable.
CMD ["lmp", "-h"]

  name: lammps-reax-mc
  namespace: default
spec:
  backoffLimit: 1
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
    launcher: false
    runFlux: true
  logging:
    strict: true
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: r7iz.8xlarge
    restartPolicy: Never
  size: 1
  tasks: 8

manager.name: Build and Deploy LAMMPS
manager.description: Build a Docker container and deploy it as a Kubernetes Job.

context.details:
Ensure all globbed files from examples/reaxff/HNS from the root of the lammps codebase are in the WORKDIR. Clone the latest branch of LAMMPS.
You MUST put lmp on the PATH.

context.optimize:
Run in.reaxff.hns in the pwd with lmp -v x 8 -v y 8 -v z 8 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite      
You MUST Minimize the lammps wall time. The resource spec you got earlier is for an autoscaling cluster,
so the nodes possible are not there. For your optimization you can choose from the following instance types,
and you will need to add the correct nodeSelector with the node.kubernetes.io/instance-type label indicating your
choice. You are still limited to one node.
  c7a.12xlarge, 48 CPU, 96 GiB Memory, AMD
  hpc7g.16xlarge, 64 CPU, 128 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton3)
  c6in.12xlarge, 24 CPU, 96 GiB Memory, Intel
  r7iz.8xlarge, 16 vCPU, 256 GiB Memory, Intel
  m6g.12xlarge, 48 vCPU, 192 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton2)
  t3a.2xlarge, 4 CPU, 32 GiB Memory, AMD
  t3.2xlarge, 4 CPU, 32 GiB Memory, Intel
  m6id.12xlarge, 24 CPU, 192 GiB Memory, Intel
  c6id.12xlarge, 24 CPU, 96 GiB Memory, Intel
  t4g.2xlarge, 8 CPU, 32 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton2)
  m6i.12xlarge, 24 CPU, 192 GiB Memory, Intel
  m6a.12xlarge, 24 CPU, 192 GiB Memory, AMD
  m7g.16xlarge, 64 CPU, 256 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton3)
  c6i.16xlarge, 32 CPU, 128 GiB Memory, Intel
  c6a.16xlarge, 32 CPU, 128 GiB Memory, AMD
  c7g.16xlarge, 64 CPU, 128 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton3)
  r6i.8xlarge, 16 CPU, 256 GiB Memory, Intel
  r6a.12xlarge, 24 CPU, 384 GiB Memory, AMD
  r7g.12xlarge, 48 CPU, 384 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton3)
  i4i.8xlarge, 16 CPU, 256 GiB Memory, Intel
  d3.4xlarge, 8 CPU, 128 GiB Memory, Intel
You MUST remember that most instances map 2vCPU to 1CPU, with the exception of Graviton.
If you choose an ARM (Graviton) instance you MUST change the flux.container.image to be
ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9. Otherwise, do not change or set it.
